key_insight: A quantum-assisted agentic DAI framework can meet hard control deadlines for hybrid microgrid dispatch while still achieving optimal cost by selecting the solver as part of the control decision.
engineering_relevance: This enables real-time orchestration of renewable-rich microgrids with storage, demand response, and dispatchable generators under strict latency constraints.
method: BDIx agents formulate each control slot as a QUBO dispatch problem.
A coordinator agent selects among quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical solvers based on learned solver-latency beliefs.
A storage valuation mechanism prices battery energy using discounted future peak value to inject intertemporal information.
evidence_signal: In a 24-hour microgrid simulation, the framework missed zero deadlines, matched the exact optimum in every slot, achieved a daily cost of 146.24 EUR, and improved cost by 4.5 percent versus no storage valuation.
watch_item: The reported QAOA results use statevector simulation, so real hardware noise and deployment overhead may affect performance and deadline compliance.
paper_title: A Quantum-Assisted Agentic Distributed Artificial Intelligence Framework for Deadline-Bounded Orchestration of Hybrid Renewable Microgrids
